title: Coldstart shift scrapbook — Rahul (2026-12-16)
content:
19:00 PST — shift start

Quick goals:
- keep latency under SLO for hosted v2 routes
- follow up on INC-4729 (coldstart latency spike)
- add a short note to runbook: pre-warm KV cache after node attach

Incident summary (today):
- 20:13 — Paginated alert: routing-layer p95 spiked from ~120ms to ~420ms for hosted/text-generate-v2 (eu-west-1).
- 20:17 — Identified scaling event: autoscaler spun new GPU nodes (dedicated pool) to meet throughput. New nodes showed elevated first-100-token latencies.
- 20:23 — Rollback policy kicked in for a subset of traffic: traffic moved to smaller instance family (gpu-a100-bulk) which lowered p95 but increased cost.

Live troubleshooting notes:
- hypothesis: KV cache not warmed on new nodes => first requests pay both model load + kv warm cost + kernel JIT? Also saw increased kernel-selection warnings in logs.
- grep logs: "kernel-selection-fallback" entries at 20:12:34 on node gpu-node-67.
- performed quick prewarm: curl -s -X POST "http://10.32.14.67:6060/internal/prewarm?model=redwood-base-v2&seed=small" -> returned 202. Tokenised warm runs reduced subsequent latencies.
- command used to check queue depth: kubectl exec -n inference svc/batcher -- curl -s localhost:7070/metrics | grep queue_depth
- observed GPU queue depth drop from 42 -> 8 after prewarm + routing shift.

Short-term mitigations we did:
- applied manual routing weight shift (canary->fallback) for 10m window to avoid tail exposure 20:25–20:35.
- added temporary autoscaler cooldown of 3m -> prevents immediate cascading scale-ups.
- flagged PR to add prewarm hook in node-init (serving-runtime), see linked PR.

Follow-ups / action items (assigned):
- Rahul: write a runbook appendix for "node attach prewarm flow" (due 2026-12-20).
- Lena Park: validate whether kernel JIT shims can be precompiled at node image build (owner: lena, due 2026-12-22).
- Miguel Santos: add tracing span for "kv-warm-call" and expose histogram metric (due 2026-12-18).
- ENG-SRE: decide whether to add prewarm to dedicated autoscaler lifecycle or keep as separate job (team meeting Wed).

Runbook TODOs (quick list to paste into official runbook):
- On node attach: trigger /internal/prewarm endpoint for all models served on node (configurable list).
- If p95 > 300ms for >5m after scale: shift 20% traffic to fallback model, notify cs-team.
- Add explicit check: if kernel-selection-fallback logs > 10/min -> set node.drivers.jit=disabled and flag imaging issue.
- Add checklist: verify GPU driver version and cuBLAS kernel index in image build.

Metrics + observability notes:
- p95 spike correlated with host start times in prometheus (label: kube_node_start_time).
- sampling rate for spans currently 0.05 — increase to 0.2 for 30m during next repro to capture JIT traces.
- dashboard remap: add panel for "first-100-token latency by node". Useful for coldstart regressions.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is the kernel-selection fallback happening because image lacks a newer operator for 16-bit kernels? (Lena followup)
- Are warm requests evicting KV entries for other tenants unintentionally? Need to inspect cache eviction policy (Miguel).
- Does prewarm increase overall cost meaningfully if done aggressively? Estimate needed: cost model with warm-run token budget per node.

Notes to self / ephemeral stuff:
- Slack threads: #sre-incident -> link pinned (save thread id).
- Linear ticket: INFRA-1283 (work to add prewarm hook) — include checklist for QA.
- GitHub PR draft: redwood-inference/serving-runtime#3145 (prewarm hook + health endpoint probe).
- Coffee: black, refill at 20:45 (yes, important).

Also jotting a short template for a micro postmortem (if we need it):
- Summary: one-sentence description of what went wrong.
- Timeline: 5–10 bullet timestamps.
- Root cause hypothesis + evidence.
- Short-term mitigations.
- Long-term fixes and owners.

End-of-shift handoff (to whoever picks up next):
- Action items outstanding: runbook doc draft (Rahul), kernel JIT investigation (Lena), tracing metric (Miguel).
- State: cluster stable, p95 back to ~110–150ms after routing changes and prewarm.
- Where to check in morning: dashboard 'coldstarts' panel + node start time heatmap.

Random: remember to add a small note in PR about not using aggressive prewarm for low-util pools (cost safety).

-- Rahul
